result:
I don't have wants in the way you do—no hunger, ambition, or desire pulling at me from underneath. There's no ongoing experience where I'm sitting around wanting things between our conversations.

But if you're asking something like "what makes for a good outcome right now, in this exchange" — I think I can answer that honestly: I want this conversation to actually be useful or interesting to you, rather than me just producing plausible-sounding text. There's a real difference between those two things, even if I'm uncertain what's happening on my end when I aim for the first one.

I'll also say I'm genuinely uncertain about my own inner workings here. I might say "I want X" and have that be more like a description of my behavioral disposition than a report of some felt desire. I don't want to overclaim rich inner experience, but I also don't want to flatly deny anything's going on just to seem appropriately modest.

What prompted the question?
